item.title: Decoupling the Coordination-Decoordination Trade-off in PVDF-Based Electrolytes via Chlorine Substitution for High-Performance Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:

Energy & Environmental Science | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Chlorine substitution in PVDF-based electrolytes decouples the coordination-decoordination trade-off, enabling simultaneous salt dissociation and Li+ transport. This resolves a long-standing design conflict in solid-state polymer electrolytes, offering a new molecular engineering strategy for high-performance solid-state lithium metal batteries.

item.description:

Energy & Environmental Science | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using terminal-to-terminal distance as a design descriptor to screen molecules, identifying a six-carbon molecule (6.46 Å) that forms bidentate anchoring. This configuration suppresses iodine shuttling, enabling stable zinc–iodine batteries. It establishes a rational engineering principle linking molecular geometry to anchoring robustness, offering a new design strategy for high-stability battery interfaces.
